chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbbād ibn Sulaymān, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:

I asked him — meaning Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام — about a man who performed the ẓuhr or the ʿaṣr salat and then broke his wudu (ablution) when he sat in the fourth rakʿah. He said: “If he had said, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ then he does not repeat it. But if he had not uttered the shahadah before breaking his wudu (ablution), then he must repeat.”

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام being asked in the narration
key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: the declaration of testimony recited in the tashahhud
key_terms.فَأَحْدَثَ: he broke ritual purity by becoming in need of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَلَا يُعِيدُ: he does not repeat the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: If someone breaks wudu (ablution) in the fourth rakʿah after the tashahhud, must he repeat the salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who breaks wudu (ablution) while seated in the fourth rakʿah of ẓuhr or ʿaṣr salat. If he had already recited the shahadah, the salat is not to be repeated; otherwise, it must be repeated.
